Rosacea is a chronic skin condition that affects the facial skin, causing persistent redness, flushing, and visible blood vessels. It can lead to small, pus-filled bumps similar to acne and can sometimes cause eye symptoms as well.

Rosacea can be triggered by internal and external factors. Your observation that it flares up upon sun exposure or alcohol consumption aligns with common triggers for this condition. Here are some other commonly encountered triggers:

- Emotional stress
- Extremes in temperature: hot or cold, windy conditions
- Heavy exercise
- Hot baths
- Corticosteroids
- Spicy foods
- Hot beverages
- Maraschino cherry liqueur (a type of liqueur)

While there's no single, definitive cure for rosacea, you can take several measures to reduce flare-ups and help control the condition:

1. **Sun Protection:** Wear sunscreen with broad-spectrum protection and an SPF of at least 30. Reapply every two hours when outdoors, especially when the weather is sunny.
